questions.question_text: A lens has focal length +0.5 m using the Cartesian sign convention. What is its power?
questions.explanation: Power P = 1/f in metres = 1/0.5 = +2 dioptres.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A lens has power -4 D. What is its focal length?
questions.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/(-4) m = -0.25 m; the negative sign indicates a diverging lens.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An object is placed at twice the focal length of a convex lens. Where is its image formed?
questions.option_c: At twice the focal length on the other side
questions.explanation: For a converging lens, an object at 2F forms a real, inverted image at 2F on the opposite side.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An object is placed between a convex lens and its principal focus. What image does the lens form?
questions.explanation: Inside the focal length a convex lens forms a virtual, erect, magnified image on the object's side.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A concave mirror forms a real image of an object placed beyond its centre of curvature. Compared with the object, the image is
questions.explanation: Beyond C, a concave mirror forms a real, inverted, smaller image between F and C.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is a convex mirror commonly used as a vehicle rear-view mirror?
questions.option_a: It reverses left and right without reducing image size
questions.option_b: It provides an erect image and a wide field of view
questions.option_c: It always forms a real enlarged image
questions.option_d: It focuses parallel rays to a real point in front
questions.explanation: A convex mirror forms virtual erect diminished images and covers a broad field.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person can see nearby objects clearly but distant road signs are blurred. Which correction is normally prescribed?
questions.explanation: Myopia is corrected with a diverging concave lens, which moves the image back onto the retina.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In hypermetropia, why does a convex spectacle lens help a nearby object be seen clearly?
questions.option_a: It diverges rays so the image moves farther behind the retina
questions.option_b: It changes the retina into a lens
questions.option_d: It converges rays before they enter the eye
questions.explanation: A converging lens supplies additional convergence so the eye can focus the near image on the retina.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: With age, a person may have difficulty focusing both near and distant objects because the eye lens loses flexibility. This condition is
questions.explanation: Presbyopia is age-related loss of accommodation, often corrected with suitable convex or bifocal lenses.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which structure changes curvature to adjust the eye's focal length during accommodation?
questions.explanation: Ciliary muscles alter the curvature and focal length of the eye lens.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In dim light the pupil becomes larger. What is the direct purpose?
questions.option_b: To increase the eye lens's refractive index
questions.option_c: To allow more light to enter the eye
questions.option_d: To change the retina into a mirror
questions.explanation: The iris changes pupil size, controlling the amount of light entering the eye.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person views a white sheet under red light. Which colour does it appear approximately?
questions.explanation: A white surface reflects the incident visible wavelengths; under red illumination the available reflected light is red.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A prism separates white light into colours mainly because
questions.option_a: its refractive index varies with wavelength
questions.option_b: all colours have identical refraction in glass
questions.option_c: the prism creates new wavelengths from darkness
questions.option_d: white light contains only one wavelength
questions.explanation: Different wavelengths refract by different amounts in a dispersive medium.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which colour deviates least when white light passes through a glass prism?
questions.explanation: In ordinary glass dispersion, red light has a longer wavelength and is refracted less than violet.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The Sun is visible shortly before it geometrically rises because of
questions.option_d: total internal reflection in the Moon
questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight, making the Sun appear slightly above its geometric position near the horizon.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Stars appear to twinkle more than planets chiefly because stars are
questions.option_d: so distant that they appear nearly point-like, making atmospheric fluctuations more noticeable
questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction varies; a point-like star's apparent brightness and position fluctuate more than an extended planetary disc.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A rainbow is seen when sunlight interacts with raindrops. Which combination is chiefly involved?
questions.option_c: Only reflection from a plane mirror
questions.explanation: Raindrops refract and disperse sunlight, with internal reflection contributing to the observed bow.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A normal eye viewing a very distant object has its ciliary muscles relatively relaxed. The eye lens is then
questions.option_b: less curved and has a longer focal length
questions.option_c: more curved and has a shorter focal length
questions.explanation: For distant vision the ciliary muscles relax, making the lens thinner and its focal length longer.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why can a concave mirror produce either a real or a virtual image depending on object position?
questions.option_a: A mirror always transmits half the light
questions.option_b: The principal focus shifts with image brightness
questions.option_c: The object may lie outside or inside the mirror's focal length
questions.option_d: The mirror changes its material when moved
questions.explanation: For an object beyond F the reflected rays converge to a real image; inside F their backward extensions form a virtual image.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A small aperture camera obscura forms an inverted image. Which principle explains the inversion?
questions.option_a: Light waves stop at the aperture
questions.option_b: The aperture acts as a convex lens
questions.option_c: The image is inverted by atmospheric refraction
questions.option_d: Light travels approximately in straight lines through the small aperture
questions.explanation: Rays from opposite parts of the object cross at the small opening, producing an inverted image.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
